home.meta.title.message: CloudGround — The hosting panel for your Ubuntu server

home.meta.description.message: One command installs the panel on your server. Every site starts with its own cache, its own PHP, its own certificate, and backups that are test-restored after every copy.

home.hero.lede.message: One command installs CloudGround. Every site starts cached, sized for the machine, isolated from the others and backed up off the server. The measurements are published, with the method.

home.measures.intro.message: Five scenarios on the same machine. The numbers are those of the published benchmark file: nothing rounded in our favour.

cg.footer.licenseLine.message: CloudGround is source-available under the {license}: free to use on your own servers.

home.result.unit.message: requests per second, mean of 3 runs

home.result.whoPhp.message: PHP and the database, on every request

home.result.methodWith.message: Method: wrk, 500 connections for 3 runs, the mean is reported. Release v0.1.0 on a 2 vCPU VPS with Ubuntu 26.04.

home.result.methodWithout.message: Method: wrk, 10 connections for 3 runs, the mean is reported. Every request goes through PHP and the database. Same machine, same page.

home.result.methodLink.message: Method and raw data in the repository’s bench/ folder

home.hero.title.message: The control panel for an Ubuntu server that measures its own sites

home.install.label.message: On a fresh server, as root:

home.install.requirements.message: Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 LTS, amd64, at least 1 GB of RAM, ports 80 and 443 free.

home.hero.verify.message: Verify the installer before you run it

home.measures.note.message: 2 vCPU VPS, Ubuntu 26.04, WooCommerce shop page, wrk on the same server, 3 runs per scenario, mean; measured on 11 October 2026. The figures hold for that machine: on your server, repeat them with the same method. Both {data} and {method} are public.

home.guard.label.message: Example of a Guard report in the panel, with notes

home.guard.note1.message: {b} of the server-time difference between staging and production, with its 95% interval.

home.guard.note2.message: {b} per page. A page that is slower with certainty stops the release: it is the only row that breaks the table.

home.guard.stopped.message: Release stopped: /cart/ is slower than production. Production was not touched.

home.guard.note3.message: {b}, and rolling back is a single command if you need to undo a publication.

home.tests.guard.when.message: Before every Safe Push from staging

home.tests.guard.method.message: Pairs of requests to the same pages on staging and production, timed on the server. The median of the difference and its 95% interval are computed.

home.tests.guard.outcome.message: A release slower than production is not published. Verdicts: pass, warning, blocked, inconclusive.

home.tests.restore.method.message: Every snapshot, encrypted and deduplicated off the server, is restored separately and checked. The restore time is measured, not estimated.

home.tests.restore.outcome.message: A backup counts only once its test restore has succeeded. The last verified one is never removed.

home.tests.isolation.when.message: For every site, when it is created

home.tests.isolation.method.message: One Unix user, one PHP-FPM master, one systemd sandbox and one database account per site. SFTP locked into the site’s folder.

home.tests.isolation.outcome.message: A compromised site cannot see the files or the database of the others.

home.tests.drift.when.message: On the files the panel manages

home.tests.drift.method.message: The panel compares the managed files with the ones it wrote. If someone changes them by hand, it reports it.

home.tests.drift.outcome.message: It overwrites nothing on its own: you choose whether to restore or keep the change.

home.tests.intro.message: Every guarantee of the panel has a check that verifies it. For each one: how it is tested, and what happens when the test fails.

home.limits.release.text.message: The latest release is {version}. Interfaces may change before 1.0.

home.limits.audit.text.message: The code has had an internal security review. No outside firm has checked it yet.

home.limits.machine.text.message: The measurements hold for a 2 vCPU VPS. The method is public: repeat it on your server.

home.limits.licence.text.message: Elastic License 2.0. Read every line that runs as root on your server; no account with us, no per-server fee.

home.limits.intro.message: A test report also says what it does not cover.

home.procedure.intro.message: Three steps, in order. The installer checks the server before it touches anything.

home.procedure.1.text.message: A freshly created Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 LTS, amd64, at least 1 GB of RAM and 10 GB of free disk, root access over SSH. The installer takes over nginx, PHP, MariaDB and SSH: use a dedicated server.

home.procedure.2.text.message: If it finds problems (system, memory, disk, ports in use) it lists them all at once and stops without touching anything. The script checks the release’s SHA-256 and the signed manifest.

home.procedure.3.text.message: At the end it prints an address {url}, valid for 24 hours, that works once. You create the administrator, then the first site.

home.terminal.line1.message: [ok] server checked: Ubuntu, memory, disk, ports
